html:
SMTO-MAN-0010 — Some SMTO Manual reference pages couldn't be built

GUID: 60024d12-f9ba-5715-b50f-6175435f8a88
Slug: docs-generated-unavailable
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: docs

What happened

  • SMTO tried to prepare its detailed reference pages, such as the error pages, but couldn't. The main Manual guides still work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For now, use the How to fix steps in this panel or the main Manual guides. Those don't depend on the reference pages that failed to build.
  2. Ask the person who manages SMTO to run the SMTO installer again, or reinstall the app, and then start SMTO again. These pages are built from files that come with SMTO, and SMTO only tries to build them once each time it starts.
  3. After SMTO restarts, wait a minute, then open the page again. The pages are built in the background shortly after SMTO starts.

What success looks like

  • The reference page opens after SMTO has been restarted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder to fix this; these pages don't come from your saved data, and that folder holds your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The generated Manual reference pages failed to load or build (missing source checkout, an unsafe or invalid cache or packaged resource, or a build error), so they report unavailable; the authored Manual is unaffected.

What this means

  • Generated loading/building fails or rejects unsafe/inconsistent cache/source content, so the lane reports unavailable without replacing the authored snapshot. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • Generated loading/building fails or rejects unsafe/inconsistent cache/source content, so the lane reports unavailable without replacing the authored snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the bounded loader/build cause and cache ownership/source consistency; unavailable is not the warming retry state.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the manual-references worker failure. For packaged installs verify the manual-references.json resource (not a symlink, at most 64 MiB, a non-empty list); for source installs verify the checkout (pyproject.toml and src/manual) and the cache at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/smto/manual/docs-v1 (default ~/.cache/smto/manual/docs-v1; owned by the server user, not a symlink). Restart the Server after the repair, because the pages are built once per process.
  • Use current authored guidance. Restart after repairing the installed build resource or source cache.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use current authored guidance. Restart after repairing the installed build resource or source cache.

How to verify the fix

  • A repaired supported build publishes a valid generated snapshot and current authored reads remain available.

What not to do

  • Do not invent references, read arbitrary files through Docs or retry in a tight loop.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
